correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, exact CTMC conditional expectations give C_j=sum c_i z_i^j. The Bernoulli square identity and independence give T_j=sum c_i(1-2pi_i) z_i^(2j). Strictly positive c_i and pairwise distinct z_i make the covariance Hankel pencil identifiable and its determinant positive. The second Vandermonde inverse uniquely restores pi_i and hence both rates. The two-patch alias has identical full mean/covariance and opposite third centered lag-one moments; exact rational finite-state enumeration of examples corroborates normalization and signs. The universal theorem rests on the analytical proof, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The general Prony exponential-sum recovery of decay factors and covariance weights is known and is not claimed. The assessed mathematical contribution is the exact third-order reconstruction of direction-specific colonization/extinction rates from only aggregate count time series, the explicit finite observation design, and the sharp two-patch failure of all stationary first- and second-order data. A full accessible 2013 ecological Markov-transition paper develops site-resolved transition inference rather than this summary-data inversion. Other inspected metadata and mathematical-record statements concern different observation models. Potential equivalent results in factorial hidden Markov/telegraph-noise literature remain an acknowledged bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A direct earlier spectral/factorial hidden-Markov or multiple-telegraph-source identifiability theorem might specialize to the exact moment-order statement; none was located in searches.
Full text of Royle–Kéry 2007 and O'Cinneide 1991 was unavailable; only abstracts were used to assess the difference of observation models.
The moment inversion may be numerically ill-conditioned for nearly equal turnover rates; no robustness theorem is claimed.

value.rationale: The natural ecological monitoring inverse question asks whether unlabeled aggregate patch-richness trajectories can reveal individual colonization and extinction mechanisms. The finding gives a complete all-size identifiability theorem and an explicit finite observation protocol under distinct relaxation, and sharply identifies the unavoidable second-order information loss already with two patches. It is not merely known Prony pole recovery: the latter leaves a genuine occupation-direction ambiguity that the temporal third cumulant resolves. Assumptions and lack of noisy-sample stability are explicit.
